nodes.prompt:
TASK: Implement clients/rust/erd-net — the complete transport layer. Four modules, TDD where seams exist.
DELIVERABLE:
1. tls_psk.rs — openssl crate (vendored feature) TLS client+server: external PSK callback (identity utf8 bytes, no null), identities 'erd-b1' (bootstrap) / 'erd-p1.<uuid>' (pairing), pin TLS1.2 PSK ciphersuites (TLS_PSK_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 / TLS_PSK_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384), min TLS1.2 max TLS1.3, verify callback always-true (PSK transcript is the auth). TLS1.3 PSK is KNOWN to fail on Apple stack — do not enable. Framing: 4B LE prefix + payload, 16MiB cap, partial-read state machine, oversized→drop.
2. udp_gcm.rs — AES-256-GCM datagram: plaintext 12B header + AEAD payload with AAD = header bytes; nonce 12B = 4B direction prefix + 8B BE counter; HKDF-SHA256 key chains byte-exact to spec (ikm 'erd/udp-ikm/v3', directions 'erd/udp-c2h/v3'/'erd/udp-h2c/v3', nonce suffix '/nonce'); 4096-packet sliding replay window with 64-block bitmask; unit tests ported from Swift CryptoProtocolTests (round-trip, tamper, AAD mismatch, duplicate, stale-outside-window, direction-keys-incompatible — port ALL 6).
3. signaling.rs — ntfy candidate exchange: topic 'erd3-'+hex(HKDF(ikm=pin, salt 'erd/signaling/v3', info 'erd/topic').prefix(14)), POST base64(AES-GCM(JSON candidate, key=HKDF(ikm=pin, salt 'erd/signaling/v3', info 'erd/payload-key'))), Content-Type text/plain, POST status check (non-2xx → error), poll GET /json?poll=1&since=10m at 1s to 10s deadline, JSONL parse .message, role filter, base64→AES-GCM open. Live test gated behind env ERD_LIVE_TESTS=1.
4. stun.rs — RFC5389 XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS against stun.l.google.com:19302, magic cookie, attribute parse.
SCOPE: contract = .omo/plans/tauri-client.md '## v3 Wire protocol spec'. Port test vectors from Tests/XCTests/CryptoProtocolTests.swift (HKDF RFC5869 A.1/A.3, DatagramCipher round-trip/tamper/AAD/duplicate/stale/direction — all 6 cases) and ERDIdentity bootstrap-lockout semantics.
VERIFY: cargo test -p erd-net all green (PSK loopback test spins an in-process openssl PSK server thread); clippy -p erd-net clean.
STOP WHEN: transport complete, tests green, clippy clean.
NOTE: openssl vendored feature on macOS — add openssl-sys vendored feature to erd-net Cargo.toml for portability.

nodes.prompt:
TASK: Implement the Rust macOS host — the server side that captures the screen, encodes, serves the v3 protocol, and injects input. Binary crate clients/rust/erd-host (bin target erd-host).
DELIVERABLE:
1. capture_macos.rs — ScreenCaptureKit via objc2-screen-capture-kit, building on the WORKING spike at crates/spike-sck/src/main.rs (reuse its proven pattern: define_class SCStreamOutput sink, DispatchQueue, completion-handler ownership rules — the autoreleased-pointer retain trick is REQUIRED). Output: BGRA IOSurface/CVPixelBuffer frames at display rate.
2. encode_vt.rs — VideoToolbox HEVC encode via FFmpeg hevc_videotoolbox (ffmpeg-next with videotoolbox feature): AVCC output (4B BE length-prefixed NALUs, VPS/SPS/PPS prepended on keyframes), bitrate control (LAN mode 50-150Mbps configurable, default 8Mbps for compatibility), queue depth 3, realtime mode.
3. inject_macos.rs — CGEvent injection via core-graphics: mouse move/down/up/drag, scroll, keyboard with modifier flags (map from the v3 input payload), coordinate mapping from normalized+host dims to CGEvent absolute pixels (CGEventPost to kCGHIDEventTap).
4. session.rs — server state machine: TCP TLS-PSK listener (openssl server-side PSK callback offering 'erd-b1' bootstrap + 'erd-p1.<uuid>' entries from the pairing file), pairing flow (pairingRequest → isPairingActive check → consent prompt via UI callback channel → grant/reject), handshake v3 gating (version=3, known pairingID, sessionSalt present → derive UDP direction keys, arm ciphers, then media allowed — refuse input/control pre-auth), heartbeat (2s ping, 3x timeout), audio capture (SCK audio output → fragmentation [frameId u32][fragIdx u16][fragCount u16]), per-frame timestamps (capture→encode→send monotonic, pushed as side-channel stats), PIN display (8-digit via the host's randomPIN), file-based pairing store (0600 JSON mirroring host convention), recordBootstrapFailure lockout on TLS failures.
5. main.rs — CLI: --bootstrap-pin <pin> / --pin generate / --list-paired / --revoke <id>; onboarding: TCC prompts (Screen Recording, Accessibility) with CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess/AXIsProcessTrusted checks and clear guidance.
SCOPE: protocol contract = .omo/plans/tauri-client.md '## v3 Wire protocol spec'. FFI reference = crates/spike-sck/src/main.rs (proven). Swift behavior reference = Sources/HostCore/*.swift + Sources/ClientCore/ClientCore.swift (server semantics).
VERIFY: cargo test -p erd-host (session state machine unit tests: pre-auth gating, lockout, key derivation); integration: host starts, displays PIN, accepts a scripted loopback pairing+handshake (write a Rust test client using erd-net); per-frame timestamps emitted.
STOP WHEN: host streams ≥10 timestamped frames to a test client over loopback with ciphers armed.
TCC: first run triggers Screen Recording + Accessibility prompts — expected; document in --help.

3. Platform audio: cpal 48kHz stereo f32 output stream from the reassembly queue.
SCOPE: protocol contract = .omo/plans/tauri-client.md '## v3 Wire protocol spec'. Swift behavior reference = Sources/ClientCore/*.swift (port semantics: pairing client flow, ABR thresholds 5%/0.75x/30s, clipboard echo suppression changeCount+hash+concealed filter, cursor handling).

DELIVERABLE:

Print PASS/FAIL summary.
2. scripts/latency-bench.sh + bench JSON output — per-frame timestamps (capture→encode→send→recv→decode→present, monotonic) aggregated p50/p99/max, plus input round-trip latency (send input event → observe host-side injection log timestamp delta). Output JSON to stdout.
3. Moonlight comparison stub — scripts/moonlight-compare.md documenting the identical test scenario for manual Moonlight measurement (same tailnet, same resolution) so numbers are comparable.
SCOPE: the Rust host (clients/rust/erd-host) and client (clients/rust/erd-app + binaries) already implement pairing (PIN bootstrap), handshake v3, encrypted UDP streaming with per-frame timestamps. VM: tart run --no-graphics eclipticrd-ci; ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 admin@$(tart ip eclipticrd-ci); the VM has Rust toolchain + repo at ~/EclipticRD. Test rule: E2E runs in the VM, never on the host Mac.
VERIFY: ./scripts/vm-interop.sh exits 0 printing 'INTEROP_PASS frames>=10'; ./scripts/latency-bench.sh prints JSON with p50/p99 for ≥30 frames.
STOP WHEN: interop passes and bench JSON is produced (commit both scripts + a sample bench JSON).

nodes.prompt:
TASK: Implement the Linux host backend for EclipticRD (target: omarchy — Arch + Hyprland + Wayland) as cfg-gated modules in clients/rust/erd-host (platform module: #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]).
DELIVERABLE:
1. capture_linux.rs — Hyprland/wlr-screencopy capture (hyprland-share or wlr-export-dmabuf protocol via wayland client crate; fastest path for Hyprland) with PipeWire portal fallback documented; output BGRA frames + damage/region info when available.
2. encode_linux.rs — VAAPI HEVC/H.264 encode (libva via ffmpeg-next vaapi hwaccel) with x264 software fallback (realtime preset, no B-frames); same AVCC-style output contract as macOS encode.
3. inject_linux.rs — uinput-based input injection (kernel-level, works on Wayland): mouse move/click/scroll, keyboard with the v3 modifier mapping, coordinate mapping to the target output; udev permissions documentation (uinput group).
4. clipboard_linux.rs — Wayland wl-clipboard (wl-copy/wl-paste CLI or protocol) + X11 fallback (xclip), echo suppression ported from the Swift semantics (changeCount analog: content hash + period), 4KB cap, concealed filter (org.nspasteboard.ConcealedType where supported).
5. audio_linux.rs — PipeWire (or PulseAudio) monitor capture for system audio, 48kHz stereo f32, same fragmentation output contract.
SCOPE: platform backends implement the same traits/interfaces the macOS backend uses (defined in N5's host core — read clients/rust/erd-host/src/ to match; if trait seams are missing, add minimal platform-trait seams WITHOUT changing macOS behavior).
VERIFY: cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu for the linux cfg modules (cross-check syntax); unit tests for non-FFI logic (keymap, normalization, clipboard hashing); CI linux job builds the workspace. Runtime QA on real Wayland is the deployment step (document in module docs).
STOP WHEN: linux-gated code compiles clean, pure-logic tests green, CI linux job green.
NOTE: do not break the macOS build — cfg-gate everything Linux-specific.

DELIVERABLE:

Code review pass: (a) unsafe blocks in FFI modules (capture_macos, encode_vt, inject) — ownership, lifetime, null-deref, thread-safety audit; (b) protocol implementation vs docs/protocol-v3.md cross-check (byte layouts, HKDF strings, PSK identities); (c) error handling — no unwraps on network/decode paths, no silent error swallowing; (d) replay window + crypto usage correctness vs spec; (e) resource leaks — threads, queues, GPU resources on teardown.
4. Deliver a review report: APPROVE or BLOCK with file:line-cited issues, each tagged CRITICAL/MAJOR/MINOR; fix CRITICAL+MAJOR issues found (in clients/rust/** only — Swift is frozen), re-run the affected gates, and re-verify.
VERIFY: all gates green after fixes; report saved to .omo/evidence/ulw/tauri-client/review-final.md.
STOP WHEN: report written with APPROVE (fixes applied for any blocker) and all gates re-run green.
